candidates.rationale: Firms whose best profitability print is recent and worst is stale are on an improving quality path investors underreact to.
Recency of the cleanest accrual quarter marks where earnings became cash-backed, which the market prices slowly.
A margin peak set long ago signals eroding pricing power; a fresh peak signals operating leverage still building.
Firms that hit their lowest leverage recently have just re-levered or are about to, a negative for equity holders.
Divergence in when turnover versus margin peaked separates volume-driven from price-driven profit cycles.
Distance since the trough EPS quarter dates the earnings recovery, and recoveries are extrapolated too slowly.
Freshly peaking book value means retained earnings just landed rather than being distributed or written down.
High current ROE is more credible when the recent trough is old, separating durable returns from a one-quarter bounce.
Profitability peaking after the accruals peak means the earnings were cash-backed rather than accrual-manufactured.
Ordering of margin and turnover troughs distinguishes cost-side from demand-side shocks, which mean-revert at different speeds.
A jump in the age of the ROE high marks the exact window where profitability rolled over, before analysts cut.
Movement in the leverage-trough clock dates new balance-sheet expansion, which precedes weaker equity returns.
Profitable firms still making new profitability highs are compounding, not peaking, so the level signal is more persistent.
Leverage topping more recently than profitability flags debt-funded growth outrunning the returns that service it.
Book troughing later than earnings indicates writedowns lagging the profit recovery, so book is understated.
Profitability high in its own recent range while leverage is low in its range is self-funded quality.
Margins at the top of their own history with accruals at the bottom means the margin expansion is cash-real.
Within-firm ranking avoids the industry tilt of a cross-sectional ROE sort while keeping the accrual-quality overlay.
Both DuPont legs improving relative to the firm's own history is the rare combination that sustains ROA.
Earnings climbing faster than book within the firm's own history is rising incremental return on equity.
Noisy profitability relative to its own level is low earnings quality and carries a persistent risk discount.
Unstable margins signal weak pricing power and cost pass-through, which the market rewards only after it is proven.
Coefficient of variation of EPS is the classic earnings-predictability measure; unpredictable earners underperform.
Rapidly moving capital structure means financing stress or aggressive M&A, both of which raise the equity's option-like risk.
Efficient firms are rewarded only when the efficiency is stable; volatile turnover is inventory or channel noise.
Swinging accruals indicate discretionary reporting, a red flag for future negative earnings surprises.
A profitability information ratio prices durable returns on assets rather than a single flattering quarter.
Margin level scaled by its own variability captures moat width, which supports returns over long horizons.
Consistently high asset utilisation reflects disciplined capital deployment that compounds slowly into returns.
Smooth, high earnings attract lower risk premia over time; the repricing is gradual and thus predictable.
The range of leverage over two years measures balance-sheet instability, which precedes distress-driven underperformance.
Wide accrual swings mark aggressive period-end reporting that later reverses through earnings.
Worst-quarter profitability is a downside-quality measure; firms that never lose money are systematically underpriced.
The floor of the margin distribution proxies cost flexibility, which protects earnings and lowers realised risk.
Trough returns paired with peak leverage is the coverage test equity holders eventually apply.
Short window above long window is a profitability trend rather than a level, so it is not a stale industry tilt.
Recent margins exceeding the multi-year average identifies the early phase of an operating-leverage cycle.
Improving asset utilisation shows demand absorbing installed capacity before it shows up in reported margins.
A rising accrual run-rate versus its own history is the deterioration in earnings quality that precedes misses.
Exponential margin crossover reacts to the newest report faster than simple averages while staying smooth.
Return on assets amplified by capital efficiency, penalised for balance-sheet risk, is unlevered quality.
Operating returns per unit of financial risk isolates firms whose profits do not depend on debt.
The ROE-to-ROA ratio is the implied equity multiplier, so high values are leverage dressed up as profitability.
Sales generated per share of book, cleaned of accrual inflation, is a cash-grounded value-quality blend.
Earnings against a smoothed book base is a stable ROE proxy immune to one-quarter book restatements.
Profitability surprise relative to the firm's own base rate is the part of the print analysts had not embedded.
Deviation from the firm's own margin history is a within-name surprise, free of sector level effects.
A step up in utilisation versus own history signals capacity tightening, which leads pricing and margins.
An accrual spike above the firm's own norm is the concrete form of the accrual anomaly, timed to the report.
Book growth funded by retention rather than issuance signals internal compounding rather than dilution.
Current EPS versus its own two-year average is a scale-free earnings momentum that survives across sectors.
A standardised profitability change is a fundamental SUE: big moves relative to a firm's own noise get underreacted to.
Scaling the margin change by its historical noise stops stable-margin firms being drowned out by cyclicals.
A statistically large efficiency improvement is an operating inflection that shows up in earnings two quarters later.
An unusually large accrual build relative to own history is where earnings management is most likely to unwind.
Rising returns with falling accruals is the cash-confirmed improvement; the two legs cancel reporting artefacts.
Equity growing while leverage falls is deleveraging by retention, a slow transfer of value to shareholders.
Margin expansion matters more at high-throughput firms because it applies to a larger revenue base.
Earnings growth from a high-margin base is more likely to persist than growth squeezed from thin margins.
Direction of the profitability change gates the margin-quality bet, avoiding value traps with deteriorating returns.
Profitability and utilisation improving together is a genuine operating inflection, not an accounting reclassification.
Margin gains achieved without adding debt are self-funded and therefore repeatable.
Accumulating profitability changes over two quarters captures the persistence, not just the latest jump.
Weighting recent margin changes most heavily times entry to the post-report drift window.
A decaying weight on efficiency changes matches the horizon over which turnover news is absorbed.
Fresh leverage increases are penalised most heavily right after they appear, when the risk repricing is incomplete.
A fast EPS change with a short decay isolates the immediate post-report reaction rather than the stale level.
Same-window return and accrual changes net out to the cash component of the newest earnings print.
Profitable firms with structurally high throughput earn their returns from operations rather than pricing luck.
High margins plus improving utilisation is the point in the cycle where incremental revenue drops to the bottom line.
Counting days above its own long-run profitability measures how entrenched the improvement is, not just its size.
Persistence of above-average margins distinguishes structural expansion from a single favourable quarter.
Sustained above-normal leverage marks firms that have not deleveraged and carry residual refinancing risk.
How often current utilisation beats last quarter's counts consecutive efficiency gains rather than one jump.
Repeatedly elevated accruals mean the reporting gap is a policy, not a timing artefact, and reverses harder.
Year-on-year ROE improvement sustained over a quarter is the fundamental analogue of persistent momentum.
When profitability is improving pay for margins; when it is deteriorating the binding constraint is the balance sheet.
Earnings deserve a positive weight only when accruals are not inflated; otherwise the same EPS predicts reversal.
Levered firms are judged on margin cushion, unlevered ones on how hard they work their assets.
Take the unlevered profitability measure whenever leverage is flattering ROE, avoiding a debt-driven quality score.
Quality net of the joint accrual and leverage risk, the two channels through which reported quality is manufactured.
DuPont operating return with a direct accrual haircut prices only the cash-backed portion of profitability.
Smoothed cash profitability over one quarter is the horizon at which the accrual correction actually plays out.
High returns earned with a stable capital structure are more repeatable than the same returns with shifting debt.
Year-on-year book accretion measures retained value creation independent of the multiple the market assigns.
Year-on-year EPS change removes seasonality in quarterly reporting, isolating true earnings growth.
Standardised year-on-year EPS growth is a fundamental surprise score that ranks comparably across volatility regimes.
Net new leverage over a year is an issuance proxy, and issuers underperform as the capital is deployed at low returns.
Year-on-year profitability improvement is slow-moving news that diffuses into prices over multiple quarters.
Quarter-on-quarter margin change is the freshest operating datapoint and is underweighted versus headline EPS.
Book to a smoothed price is a value signal that avoids anchoring on one noisy closing print.
Earnings against the quarter's peak price measures yield at the most optimistic valuation the market recently paid.
Book relative to the yearly high finds firms whose asset base is intact but whose price has de-rated hardest.
Yield measured off the recent low flags names where the market already priced a bad case that earnings did not confirm.
Cheap book is only attractive when the assets earn a margin; the product screens out asset-heavy value traps.
Quality-weighted book yield on a split-adjusted price base prices profitable assets rather than accounting bulk.
Earnings yield struck at the day's low is the yield available to a patient buyer, and intraday lows are where value trades.
Book against the average of recent lows measures downside-anchored value, less sensitive to melt-ups.
Earnings yield tilted toward capital-efficient firms, since efficiency makes the earnings stream more durable.
Profitable book bought cheaply combines the value and quality premia that historically offset each other's drawdowns.
Cash earnings yield, subtracting the accrual component that will not repeat, is the version of E/P that predicts.
Book yield adjusted for soft assets prices only the portion of equity backed by realised cash.
Cheap on a long-run price base but not through balance-sheet risk separates value from distress.
Value only pays where operations are profitable; the interaction prices cheapness conditional on business quality.
Both legs smoothed over the same quarter aligns the stale fundamental with a comparably stale price.
Matching averaging windows on earnings and price removes the artificial turnover caused by daily price moves alone.
Book accretion per dollar of price is retained-earnings yield, which compounds into returns without needing a re-rating.
Earnings growth scaled by price is the change in earnings yield, the part of growth investors are actually paid for.
Buy profitable firms whose price has not yet run relative to its own trend, a quality-minus-re-rating spread.
Margin quality net of price extension buys the same business quality at a lower point in the price cycle.
High earnings yield backed by asset efficiency is cheapness with an operating reason, not a broken business.
Cheap against recent highs and clean on accruals is value the accounting is not exaggerating.
Return on equity times book over price is an earnings yield built from the balance sheet rather than reported EPS.
Operating return per dollar of market price is an unlevered yield that ignores capital-structure distortions.
Cheap book with a clean balance sheet is the low-distress corner of value where the premium actually accrues.
Yield conditioned on sustained profitability screens the cheap names whose earnings base is genuine.
Cheap and low volatility is value without the risk-loading that explains away most of the raw value spread.
Earnings yield net of realised risk isolates cheapness that is not compensation for volatility.
Profitable book relative to traded value flags quality that is under-traded and therefore under-followed.
Cheap and thinly traded is where limits to arbitrage let the earnings-yield premium survive.
Profitability per unit of equity volatility is a fundamental Sharpe ratio; the market underpays for low-risk quality.
Stable-margin firms with quiet stocks are the low-beta quality names that earn positive alpha against CAPM.
Operating efficiency relative to price noise finds businesses whose fundamentals move more than their quotes.
Leverage and equity volatility multiply into distress risk, the combination that drives the worst realised returns.
Soft accounting in an already volatile name is where negative surprises are both likelier and more violently priced.
High returns on equity in quiet stocks is the defensive-quality trade that compounds through drawdowns.
Margin quality without recent tail moves screens out firms where an event has already changed the fundamentals.
Profitable firms with wide trading ranges are quality that is being priced with unusual disagreement.
Efficient operations plus steady trading identifies stable shareholder bases that hold through the fundamental cycle.
Cheap names with rising trading instability are where the repricing of value is starting rather than finished.
Volume waking up on a profitable name marks the arrival of attention that a quality signal needs to be priced.
Quality names where price rises on volume are seeing genuine accumulation rather than drift on thin trade.
Cheap stocks trading with return-volume alignment are being repriced by informed flow, not noise.
Accrual-heavy names get punished fastest once liquidity and attention arrive to enforce the correction.
Quality plus a stale liquidity peak means the crowd has already left, leaving fundamentals to reassert themselves.
A high-margin firm whose price low is recent has a fundamentals-price gap that closes as the panic fades.
Cheap on book with the price trough well behind it is value that has already stopped falling.
Profitability confirmed by the stock sitting high in its own price range is quality the market has begun to accept.
Long quality that the price range has not yet recognised, short the reverse, is a fundamentals-versus-price gap trade.
Margin strength minus price-range strength buys quality before the re-rating rather than after it.
Efficient operators whose stock has lagged a quarter are the clearest fundamental-versus-price dislocations.
Profitable names that pulled back on no fundamental change are where reversal and quality reinforce each other.
Cheapness that got cheaper without an earnings cut is a mispricing rather than an information event.
Improving fundamentals with a falling price is the widest gap between the accounting and the market's view.
Margin improvement not yet paid for by the stock is under-reaction to fundamental news over the same window.
Year-long earnings growth against year-long price return isolates growth the market has not capitalised.
Book compounding faster than price mechanically raises book yield, which subsequently mean-reverts upward.
Operating improvement bought during a price drawdown gets both the fundamental gain and the reversal.
Stocks that rallied while adding debt have priced the growth but not the added claim ahead of shareholders.
Overnight-to-close reversal is stronger in high-quality names because the drop is less likely to be information.
Three-day reversal conditioned on margin quality distinguishes liquidity-driven dips from fundamental repricing.
Short-term reversal pays most in cheap names where a valuation floor limits how far the drop can be justified.
High-ROE stocks that just underperformed are supported by fundamentals while the flow pressure unwinds.
A short pop in an accrual-heavy name is the best moment to fade, since the accounting will not confirm it.
Efficient firms recover faster from three-day price dislocations because their cash generation is unaffected.
Cheap names without a recent return spike are dislocations with no news, which revert rather than trend.
Intraday buying pressure in quality names reflects informed accumulation that continues into the next session.
Closing near the day's high in a profitable name shows demand absorbing supply, which persists overnight.
Levered names that fade off the high are where risk-off flow hits hardest the following day.
A volume surge on a cheap stock is the start of the value repricing, and volume shifts daily.
Attention arriving at a quality name is what converts a slow fundamental edge into realised return.
Volume spikes are when the accrual correction is enforced, so weight the short by contemporaneous activity.
Accelerating volume in a high-margin name flags position building ahead of the next report.
Cheap plus heavily traded today is value being actively discovered rather than value quietly ignored.
Trading above the closing price in a quality name indicates buyer-initiated flow within the session.
Efficient firms whose price is easily moved per dollar traded offer the largest illiquidity-plus-quality premium.
Quality names trading unusually quietly are being ignored, and the quality signal decays slower when unnoticed.
Fade short-term moves only in firms whose profitability outweighs their debt; elsewhere let the move run.
When accruals are elevated, trade against the price move; otherwise trust the profitability level.
In stressed regimes pay for margin cushion; in calm regimes pay for cheapness, which needs time to work.
On busy days the quality signal is priced; on quiet days the accrual short is the one that still pays.
Above trend, quality leads; below trend, valuation support leads, matching how the two premia alternate.
After a rally the market pays for profitability, after a drawdown it pays for asset backing.
Momentum is trustworthy when fundamentals are improving and is otherwise a candidate for reversal.
For newly levered firms volatility is the binding risk; for the rest, profitability is the payoff driver.
Stocks whose price tracks their own profitability are efficiently followed; those that do not carry a lagged edge.
A price that follows accruals rather than cash earnings is being fooled by the accounting, and later corrects.
Volume responding to margin changes marks names where fundamental news actually reaches the tape.
A low earnings-price correlation identifies stocks trading on sentiment, where the fundamental signal is unpriced.
Prices rising with leverage means the market is capitalising debt-funded expansion that has yet to earn its cost.
Returns that co-move with profitability news indicate the fundamental channel is live in this name.
Book growth attracting traded value shows the equity issuance or accretion is being noticed and repriced.
Volatility reacting to utilisation changes identifies operating-leverage names whose fundamentals drive the risk.
Quality names whose worst day is behind them have absorbed the shock and resume their fundamental drift.
A margin-strong name whose volume peak is old is under-owned relative to the fundamentals it now reports.
Cheap stocks whose price peak is stale have de-rated on time, not news, which is the recoverable kind.
Levered firms that recently set new lows are the ones where refinancing risk is actively repricing.
Cash profitability in a stock that has lagged half a year is quality on sale after non-fundamental selling.
Clean margins in a volatile stock pay most because the risk premium overstates the true fundamental risk.
Unlevered profitability combined with a monthly pullback is a fundamentally supported reversal entry.
Cash-backed efficiency plus rising participation is the setup where fundamental quality gets repriced quickly.
A profitability change confirmed by unusual volume is news the market is actively absorbing right now.
Fresh margin news weighted by same-day traded value times the drift to when it is actually being priced.
The earnings print times the volume reaction to it separates confirmed surprises from ignored ones.
A brand new leverage increase in an already volatile stock is the fastest-acting distress signal available.
A fresh accrual build with a price that has not yet fallen marks the correction that has not started.
Profitability news scaled by equity volatility measures the surprise in units the market actually trades in.
The book value jump at the report, scaled by price, is an immediate change in book yield priced with a lag.
Margin news minus the concurrent price move is the unpriced residual of the report over the same days.
Return-on-equity news the price has not chased in three days is short-horizon fundamental under-reaction.
Efficiency news arriving on a down day is the cleanest moment to accumulate on an improving operator.
Direction of the newest earnings change gates a short reversal, buying dips only after good news.
Recent price strength is faded when accruals just rose and followed when they just fell.
Quality-weighted recent returns accumulate the drift that profitable firms earn during their post-report window.
Accrual-weighted trailing returns identify the rallies most likely to be given back as the accounting normalises.
High-margin firms with recent price activity are quality names in the middle of being repriced.
Profitability-weighted share of directional movement measures how much of the price path was quality-driven.
Volume-weighted profitability captures the quality level at which shares actually changed hands.
Earnings per dollar traded is a turnover-adjusted yield that rises when a cheap name goes quiet.
Book per dollar traded net of leverage is cheapness on a flow basis without the distress component.
Profitability divided by price via the traded-value identity gives a quality yield that updates daily.
A daily-refreshed earnings yield combined with a two-week pullback times the entry into cheap names.
Margin scaled by inverse price prices quality per dollar of share price, which rises as the stock falls.
Profitability per unit of recent price range rewards quality that is not already being violently repriced.
Margins relative to typical daily range measures fundamental stability against market-implied uncertainty.
Book value against the year's trading range flags asset backing large relative to the market's uncertainty.
Debt load relative to price range is a crude distance-to-default: high values are quiet stocks carrying hidden risk.
Quality names where volume and volatility move together are those with an active information flow.
Accrual-heavy names being bought on rising volume are crowded positions with weak accounting support.
Efficient operators that have drifted down over a month recover as operating cash flow reasserts value.
Compounded quality bought after six months of underperformance is the classic quality-at-a-discount entry.
Profitable firms whose worst daily loss was mild have limited tail risk, which the market prices too slowly.
Quality without a large event move over a year is a business the market has had no reason to reassess.
Cheap names with a high share of up days are value where the tape has already turned.
Profitable firms with a positive up-day balance combine fundamental support with persistent buying pressure.
Aggressive accruals with a strong recent up-day balance is a crowded uptrend without accounting support.
Margin quality confirmed by signed dollar flow shows institutions accumulating the fundamentally stronger names.
Buy quality that flow has not yet chased and sell quality already crowded by signed volume.
Cheap and losing attention is where the value premium is largest because arbitrage capital has left.
Profitable book value in less-traded names captures quality plus the liquidity premium that keeps it unpriced.
High margins among smaller traded names is quality where coverage is thin and adjustment is slow.
Efficient firms with stable trading intensity have no flow shocks masking the fundamental drift.
Sustained profitability in a name whose liquidity is high in its own history gets repriced without impact costs.
Quality currently ignored by volume is where the delayed-reaction component of the quality premium sits.
Returns per unit of combined financial and market risk is a risk-adjusted quality score, not a raw level.
Profitability discounted by both leverage and price noise avoids paying for returns bought with risk.
Unlevered operating return per unit of equity volatility is the cleanest quality-per-risk ranking available here.
Long-run profitability minus long-run volatility is the defensive-quality composite that earns a persistent premium.
Structural margin strength against structural price noise separates stable franchises from cyclical ones.
Efficient operations with a narrow relative trading range is quality the market treats as uncontroversial.
Profitable firms whose price trend has already turned up combine confirmed quality with early re-rating.
Margin quality gated on a smoothed trend avoids buying deteriorating businesses that merely look cheap.
Book against an exponentially weighted price reacts faster to a de-rating than a flat average does.
Smoothed earnings yield cleaned of accrual inflation is cash cheapness measured against a stable price base.
Operating output per dollar of price is a throughput yield that value screens on book alone miss.
Improving profitability in an already cheap stock is the combination where re-rating and earnings both contribute.
Year-long margin improvement plus a high earnings yield is quality improvement the price has not paid for.
Utilisation gains outrunning price gains identifies operating improvement still absent from the valuation.
Book accretion measured in units of price volatility is fundamental progress relative to the market's noise band.
Earnings change against typical daily range says whether the news is large compared to normal price moves.
Debt added per dollar of price is the dilution of the equity claim, which erodes returns over the following year.
A within-firm profitability surprise combined with a monthly price pullback is under-reaction with an entry point.
Margin surprise confirmed by unusual volume is the report the market is currently digesting.
An accrual spike alongside a price rally is the most fragile configuration in the accounting-anomaly literature.
Quality with the price trough behind it, penalised for debt, is a fundamentally screened recovery trade.
Book value against the worst price of the year, cleaned of soft accounting, measures hard downside support.
Earnings yield at peak valuation, filtered on margins, finds quality that has de-rated without deteriorating.
Price extension is only worth following where accruals are clean; otherwise the trend lacks earnings support.
Quality minus short-term price extension buys the fundamentally strong names before the crowd arrives.
High-margin names whose recent floor holds above the long-run average show fundamental support in the tape.
Book yield multiplied by the return earned on that book prices the compounding rate, not just the discount.
Earnings yield weighted by margin quality favours cheap firms whose profits come from durable pricing power.
Combined asset and flow yield is a broader value composite that is less sensitive to accounting mix by industry.
Cash earnings yield in an efficient operator is cheapness backed by both the cash flow and the operating engine.
A four-way quality composite nets profitability and efficiency against the accounting and financing risks.
Two profitability legs minus realised risk is defensive quality built from independent measurement channels.
Level plus change in profitability pays for both established quality and the improvement still being priced.
Combining margin level and margin trend captures firms that are both good and getting better.
Efficiency level and trend, net of leverage, isolates operational improvement not bought with the balance sheet.
Multiplying quality ranks requires all three legs to agree, which sharply reduces false positives from one metric.
Taking the weaker of two quality ranks enforces a floor, so a single flattering metric cannot carry the score.
Weakest-link quality combined with clean accruals is a conservative screen that avoids accounting-driven scores.
Shorting on the worse of the two risk measures catches firms failing on either accounting or financing grounds.
The better of two profitability measures with a concave transform keeps ordering while damping outlier quarters.
Winsorising both legs stops a handful of extreme accounting values dominating the cross-sectional score.
Bounded accruals rank the anomaly without letting restatement outliers set the whole short book.
Log book minus log price is book-to-price in additive form, which is better behaved when either leg is small.
Log earnings yield with the sign restored ranks loss-makers correctly instead of mixing them with cheap winners.
Squaring the ranks concentrates the bet in the extremes, where the quality and leverage effects are strongest.
Profitability is only rewarded while book is still growing; shrinking book means the returns are being paid out or lost.
Margin quality gated on the direction of utilisation avoids margins that are being held up by shrinking volume.
Cheapness is a trap when profitability is falling; the sign gate removes the deteriorating half of the value book.
Cheap book only pays where leverage is falling, since rising debt is how book yield turns into distress.
Quality aligned with the twelve-month price trend combines a slow fundamental with slow price confirmation.
Throughput matters most when margins are improving, because incremental units then carry incremental profit.
Short minus long profitability average is a pure fundamental trend that is orthogonal to the level ranking.
Accruals falling versus their own history is quietly improving earnings quality that no headline reports.
A fast-versus-slow exponential profitability crossover reacts on the report date rather than a window later.
Exponential EPS crossover dates the earnings inflection precisely enough to trade the post-report drift.
Efficiency crossover marks the point where capacity utilisation starts running ahead of the installed base.
An upward leverage crossover is the earliest visible sign of balance-sheet expansion, which precedes weak returns.
Smoothed margin strength in a stock with smoothed low volatility is the persistent low-risk quality bet.
Fundamental return earned versus market return delivered flags where the gap has not yet been arbitraged.
Profits per unit of accrual is a direct cash-conversion ratio, the mechanism behind the accrual anomaly.
Margin accumulated per unit of accrual distinguishes cash margins from reporting-driven margins.
Cumulative earnings over cumulative book is a smoothed ROE that ignores single-quarter balance-sheet noise.
Accumulated profitability against accumulated leverage is the multi-year version of unlevered quality.
Distance below its own best profitability measures how much recovery is available if the firm mean-reverts.
Margins far below their own ceiling usually signal structural erosion rather than a cyclical dip to be bought.
Distance above the profitability trough dates how far into the recovery the firm already is.
Position of current margin within its own multi-year range is a scale-free fundamental oscillator.
Normalising profitability into its own historical band makes cross-sectional comparison possible without sector bias.
Leverage sitting at the top of its own historical band is where incremental debt capacity has run out.
Book value standardised above its own floor measures retained-earnings progress in units of its own variability.
Current utilisation relative to its own peak says how much slack capacity remains before margins compress.
Earnings versus their own peak identifies firms trading below prior earnings power, the base for recovery.
Recovering returns on equity in a cheap stock is where earnings recovery and multiple expansion overlap.
Profitability running above its own base while the stock lagged is a measurable gap between books and price.
Profitability improving faster than accruals means the improvement is showing up in cash, so it persists.
Margin expansion net of accrual build is the cash margin change, which is what future earnings follow.
Efficiency rising while debt falls is organic improvement rather than growth purchased with the balance sheet.
Book growth net of accrual growth is the portion of equity accretion backed by realised cash.
Return improvement is credited only when utilisation moves the same way, filtering out margin-only accounting gains.
Margin gains achieved while deleveraging are the highest-quality form of operating improvement.
Volatile profitability is survivable without debt, so the same earnings noise carries very different risk by leverage.
Margin volatility multiplied by leverage is the operating-plus-financial risk product that drives default risk.
Volatile earnings on a levered balance sheet is the configuration where covenants bind and equity gets wiped.
Profitability per unit of earnings noise and financial risk is a fundamental distance-to-default proxy.
Margin consistency net of leverage identifies firms whose earnings stability is real rather than financed.
Names whose returns already track profitability leave less unpriced fundamental information than names that do not.
Volatility rising with leverage confirms the market is pricing the debt as risk, and that repricing continues.
Volume responding to margin moves identifies the names where fundamental news drives the order flow.
Co-movement of profitability changes with price changes measures how efficiently fundamentals are transmitted.
Prices moving with accrual changes rather than cash earnings marks the mispricing that later unwinds.
Quality names whose volatility is rising are being repriced for risk, which temporarily overwhelms the fundamentals.
Margin quality with fading volume is the under-followed corner where slow-moving signals still have room to work.
Cheap names whose relative volume is turning up mark the start of the flow that closes the valuation gap.
Compounded quality in a stock whose quietest day is recent is a fundamentally strong name with no active news.
Operating return minus recent volatility acceleration buys quality before risk premia rise against it.
Cheap and unusually calm is value with no active bad news, the configuration where the discount is unjustified.
Profitable names where price and smoothed volume move together are seeing durable rather than one-day accumulation.
Recent relative volume, decayed, tells whether the quality signal is currently being acted on by the market.
Short decayed momentum inside high-margin names rides the post-report drift that quality firms exhibit.
Levered names that have been running are the first to give back gains when risk appetite turns.
Cash profitability plus a week-long decayed pullback is a high-frequency entry into fundamentally sound names.
Sales-generating book bought cheap on a down day couples a slow value signal with a one-day liquidity discount.
Long-run profitability filtered to names that just sold off is quality bought during transient supply pressure.
Structural margin strength combined with a mild worst day this week avoids catching genuine bad news.
Quality with short-term price strength and low debt is fundamentals and flow agreeing at a tradable horizon.
Margin quality with today's volume high in its recent range, net of accruals, is quality being noticed now.
Cheap names whose volume peak is very recent are in the first days of a repricing event.
Quality with the volume trough just behind it means participation is turning up from a low base.
Efficient operators seeing a jump in traded value are where new information is entering the price this week.
A sudden volume burst in an accrual-heavy name is often the start of the correction, so weight the short there.
Pay for earnings yield only when profits exceed accruals; otherwise the tradable signal is balance-sheet risk.
Follow the trend where margins are improving and fade it where they are not, since only one has fundamental support.
Growing book means judge on profitability; shrinking book means the survival question dominates.
When attention is high the market prices quality; when it fades the mispricing that persists is valuation.
On strong days short the aggressive accounting; on weak days buy the profitability, matching how each is priced.
Rising short-horizon volatility makes leverage the dominant risk; calm markets let operating efficiency pay.
Momentum is faded when accruals outrank profitability, since that trend is not backed by cash earnings.
At a fresh breakout the accounting risk dominates; away from highs, plain profitability is the better bet.
Quality names whose trading range is narrowing are settling down, letting the fundamental signal dominate returns.
High-margin names sitting near the top of their two-week range have flow confirming the fundamental story.
Gaps in cheap stocks are usually flow rather than news, so the valuation anchor makes them revert.
Very short cumulative weakness in profitable names is a liquidity discount that the fundamentals will close.
Earnings yield scaled by the return earned on equity prices both the discount and the reinvestment rate.
Book yield multiplied by the full DuPont operating chain is cheap assets that actually produce operating profit.
Profitable book yield net of realised volatility separates the value premium from its risk compensation.
